name: slack
description: Read and post in Slack with the user's workspace bot or user token. Load when a task involves Slack messages, channels, or users.

content.inline:
## Slack
Calls go through `v/ops/http/get` / `v/ops/http/post` against `https://slack.com/api/<method>` with `bearerSecret: "s/SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"` (an `xoxb-` bot token, or `s/SLACK_USER_TOKEN` for an `xoxp-` user token when the task needs the user's own view, such as search). The token comes from a Slack app the user created and installed in their workspace (api.slack.com/apps, optionally from a manifest). Only the secret reference goes in the request.

Common methods:
- Post a message: `POST chat.postMessage` headers `{"Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"}` body `{channel, text, thread_ts?, blocks?}`
- List channels: `GET conversations.list?types=public_channel,private_channel&limit=200` (paginate with `cursor`)
- Read history: `GET conversations.history?channel=C123&limit=50` (the bot must be a member; `conversations.join` for public channels)
- Users: `GET users.list`, `GET users.info?user=U123`
- Search (user token only): `GET search.messages?query=...`
- Files: `GET files.list`; uploading needs `files.getUploadURLExternal` then `files.completeUploadExternal`

Rules:
- Every response has `ok`; when `ok` is false, `error` names the cause (`missing_scope`, `not_in_channel`, `channel_not_found`). Report the scope or membership needed rather than retrying.
- Channel ids (`C...`) and user ids (`U...`) are stable; names change. Resolve names to ids once, then use ids.
- Mentions are `<@U123>`; links are `<https://url|text>`; keep messages short and thread replies with `thread_ts`.
- Rate limits are per method tier; on HTTP 429 honour `Retry-After`.
- Posting is visible to real people: confirm channel and content before `chat.postMessage` unless the task explicitly authorises posting.
